note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/api/a2a.reason: cinatra#2981 (PR #2987 carries this record): the trigger claim is ONE transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock that the stop, the save, the release job's fire decisions and the PM handler all take, and the point of #2981 is that there is exactly one of it, so it lives in one module: packages/agents/src/trigger-claim.ts. packages/agents/src/trigger-service.ts, already inside the graph this route reaches on main and already "server-only", imports withTriggerClaim and TriggerClaimUnavailableError from it as RUNTIME values, so that leaf becomes reachable and the count is +1. The growth is the module itself and nothing else: its "pg" and "server-only" imports are third-party (outside the first-party graph this metric counts), and its only first-party import, ./trigger-store, is already reachable on main. That is why every affected route moves by exactly +1, and why /sign-in, which does not reach the trigger service, does not move at all. MEASURED THE WAY CI MEASURES, with the companion extension fleet cloned pinned (112/112, missingCount 0), on two trees analysed by an identical scripts/route-graph.mjs (this PR touches only packages/agents): origin/main at 86dc699b7db4422815d1f6952f2f1cf3e51b4888 reproduces this route's previous ceiling EXACTLY, this branch's head at 81ac7828d551b3ed8a92562a93abf58625911c50 measures one higher, and the whole delta sits in the @cinatra-ai/agents owner bucket. NOT NARROWABLE, which is why this is absorbed rather than fixed structurally: the claim has to run where the decisions run; the module is already a single-purpose leaf whose only first-party dependency is already in the graph, so splitting it further would ADD modules; a computed dynamic-import seam is not a narrowing at all, because scripts/route-graph.mjs follows only LITERAL import specifiers, so such a seam would not shrink the graph, it would merely hide this edge from the metric while adding a runtime-loading boundary that has no reason to exist (and note that scripts/audit/no-variable-url-dynamic-import.mjs scans src/** only, so nothing would catch it here -- which is why it is named and rejected rather than quietly avoided); and inlining the primitive into one caller would hold the count flat only by making the release job depend on the trigger service and burying a lock primitive inside it, which is the layering inversion the one-claim design exists to prevent. No new boundary is crossed: both callers were already server-only and already reachable from this route before this PR.

Neither module imports a barrel; each edge is one module.
